title: Adaptive watermarking and late-arrival compensator for console metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: the current metrics stream pipeline assumes strict event-time ordering and fixed watermarks which fails for multi-region tenants and intermittent mobile clients. We observe percentile jumps and missing per-tenant aggregations when late events arrive (mobile jitter, network retries, clock skew). Goals: 1) reduce incorrect high-latency spikes reported to customers, 2) maintain bounded state retention and CPU cost, 3) keep end-to-end latency within SLO for 95th percentile under normal load. Approach: implement an adaptive watermarking component that adjusts lateness windows per-tenant based on observed event-time skew and ingest jitter. Introduce a late-arrival compensator stage that can re-emit corrected aggregations (deltas) for windows already emitted, with idempotent semantics. Pipeline model: hybrid queue+stream ingress -> dynamic ingress buffer (per-tenant) -> adaptive watermark calculator -> windowed aggregator with compensator -> storage / metric exporter. This work touches state management (RocksDB), checkpointing, and operator lifecycle for scaling. Trade-offs considered: increasing fixed lateness window reduces retractions but increases state and memory; compensator adds complexity but keeps normal latency low while providing correctness for late arrivals.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive watermarking deployed to canary and observed to reduce false 99th percentile spikes by >=30% for tenants with high jitter
Late-arrival compensator successfully emits idempotent correction messages and dashboard shows corrected windows in Grafana within 2 minutes of arrival
Per-tenant state growth remains bounded (no >2x increase) under synthetic late arrival test
End-to-end 95th percentile write-to-export latency stays within existing SLO (<=1.8s) under baseline load
Monitoring/alerts added for watermark drift, compensator-retry-failure, and per-tenant state growth
steps: Design doc and data model: write Confluence spec with algorithm and operator contract
Prototype adaptive watermark calculator as a library callable from both Flink and the new stream runtime
Add per-tenant ingress buffer with configurable retention and eviction policy
Implement compensator stage that records last-emitted window checksums and can produce correction deltas
Integrate idempotent keys into metric exporter and downstream datastore
Create synthetic workload harness to inject controlled lateness patterns
Canary deploy to staging region (us-west-2) with small tenant subset
Run 2-week soak, tune parameters, document operational runbooks, then roll to production
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after multiple customer incidents where per-tenant 99th percentile latency spikes corresponded to late-arriving client events. Linked incident notes and stack traces in Confluence.

2026-03-03 - Marco Hernandez: Spike analysis shows ~12% of tenants experience >5s tail on certain days. Proposal: adaptive watermarks using EWMA of event-time lag + percentile-based guardrails. Draft design uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Watermarking+Spec

2026-03-04 - Review by Priya Singh (SRE): Concern about RocksDB memory growth; suggested soft limits + eviction and telemetry to track per-tenant state. Added state.pruning and eviction parameters to design.

2026-03-06 - Marco Hernandez: Prototype implemented in local Flink job. Early results: reduced retractions by 38% for test tenants; memory increased by 18% using retention=30s. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming/pull/1245
2026-03-07 - Design feedback (Data Platform): recommended compensator idempotency be based on window-checksum + sequence number; avoid global coordination. Updated spec accordingly.

2026-03-08 - QA: synthetic harness ready. Test plan includes injecting 500ms-10s skew distributions and verifying corrections and state bounds. Link to harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming/tree/main/test/harness/late-arrivals
2026-03-09 - Canaries scheduled for 2026-03-11 in staging; engineering will monitor grafana board 'Metrics Pipeline: Watermarking' dashboard (grafana.redwood.ai/d/metrics-pipeline) during rollout

2026-03-10 - Marco Hernandez: Flagged a backpressure interaction when compensator retries; adding leaky-bucket rate limiter per-tenant for compensator emission to avoid cascading pressure on downstream exporters
rollback_plan: If canary shows state growth >2x or compensator errors >1% of emitted corrections, immediately rollback to previous operator version, disable compensator stage via runtime flag, and increase fixed lateness window to safe default (30s). Notify customers and trigger postmortem if SLA breaches occur.
operational_runbook: Runbook created in Confluence: detection queries for watermark drift, compensator error rates, restart instructions for stateful operator, and steps to clear stuck state. Pager on-call if compensator-failure-rate >0.5% for 10m.
notes: We purposely avoided global coordination for window retractions to keep system scalable across tenants.
Future iteration: consider sketch-based per-tenant state summaries to reduce RocksDB footprint for very large tenants.
Related work: ties into ENG-41209 (checkpointing improvements) and ENG-54123 (low-jitter ingress gateway)
